[0] [0] Sounds pretty interesting. ChatGPT's latest update adds a Mac integration feature: it can handle conversations from Apple's "Messages" app. This feature supports iMessage, SMS, and RCS.

[1] [1] ChatGPT for Mac now has an Apple "Messages" plugin added

[2] [2] The brand-new Apple "Messages" plugin allows ChatGPT to read and search conversation history on Mac, as well as prepare and send messages. OpenAI says this feature is available across all plans on the macOS version of the ChatGPT desktop app, with support for ChatGPT Work and Codex as well.

[3] [3] This kind of access inevitably raises concerns about privacy and control, so OpenAI emphasises that sending messages still requires user approval by default. Users should think carefully before granting persistent approval permissions. OpenAI's plugin guidelines detail the related risks, how to revoke permissions, and a known issue involving a task that disables the approval prompt.

[4] [4] Here's more from the launch announcement:

[5] [5] Additionally, OpenAI has explained in detail how the "Messages" feature works on their dedicated plugin site:

[6] [6] For now, this feature only works on Macs equipped with Apple Silicon; Intel machines are not yet supported.

[7] [7] If you ask ChatGPT to send a message on your behalf, a confirmation prompt will pop up before anything goes out. You can also choose to skip the confirmation step in individual conversations.

[8] [8] Want to find this new feature in ChatGPT? This link should jump straight to the "Messages" plugin in the Mac version of ChatGPT.

[9] [9] Site co-editing, shared conversation snapshots, and more

[10] [10] Although the "Messages" plugin is the most eye-catching new feature for Apple users, this update also includes several other improvements. For example, pinned conversations can now sync between the ChatGPT desktop app and iOS, allowing users to revisit important conversations anytime between Mac and iPhone.

[11] [11] ChatGPT can now also let users share read-only snapshots of local Codex conversations. These snapshots won't change as the original conversation is updated.

[12] [12] Links created from personal accounts can be accessed by anyone with the URL; workspace links, however, remain restricted to members of that workspace. OpenAI says Codex will mask known sensitive data patterns, but reminds users to review snapshots themselves, as sensitive information may still remain.

[13] [13] Additionally, Site owners can invite active members of the same workspace to co-edit Sites that support collaboration. Editors can update content and database data, save versions, and publish changes after the owner completes the initial publish. Owners retain final control over access, settings, analytics, and version rollback.

[14] [14] Some Site owners can also change the URL hosted by ChatGPT without needing to redeploy, with the old URL automatically redirecting to the new one.

[15] [15] Finally, the "Computer Use History" feature launched last week will be expanded to Pro, Business, and Enterprise users in the European Economic Area, Switzerland, and the UK. This optional feature requires "Memories" to be enabled and is off by default.

[16] [16] You can see the full launch announcement for this update here.
